shot_brief: A ~13.5s two-path race dramatizing the same $20,000 lead going to two contractors. It opens on a single eyebrow line ('A $20,000 LEAD COMES IN.') with a small lead icon, then splits into two simultaneous compare-card lanes (Contractor A left/muted, Contractor B right/gold) whose clocks tick in parallel at very different speeds — Lane A crawls to 'NEXT DAY' while Lane B races to '9 MINUTES' and stacks three checkmarks for answering, proof, and next steps. Both lanes land their verdict stamp on the same beat (muted '✕ LOST THE JOB' vs glowing gold '✓ BOOKED THE JOB'), hold together, then a closing line fades in beneath: 'SPEED MAKES THEM FEEL SAFE.' The piece never clears to blank — a persistent full-bleed bg-fill (matching sibling projects) covers the whole duration, scene-hook crossfades under scene-race's entrance (1.6–2.0s overlap) instead of hard-cutting, and scene-race never empties before scene-close's caption fades in beneath it (accumulating, not replacing). The dominant motif is the parallel race itself — both lanes animate in lockstep so the contrast lands as a single moment, not two sequential beats.
